rv.q: Though the piece is slow to start and overwritten in places, it is at heart a tender piece about love and loss.
Its cinematic staging creates a gloriously detailed shop-world that’s gradually dismantled, piece by piece, to leave only desolation.
For me, though, the play's emotional impact is weakened by its whimsy.
But while persuasively staged, the script meanders like the Captain lost on a snowy hillside.

The integrity of these performances roots the tragicomedy in humanity, enabling us to empathise with the characters despite the toughness of the story and the frigidity of the imagined stage world.
The script is rich in language and content, supported by excellent performances and a beautiful set.

cn.t: Thomas's metaphysical Welsh drama divides critics with its Beckettian bleakness and abstract storytelling, though most praise its strange, transfixing quality and Ifans' tender performance as a shopkeeper clinging to memory in a post-apocalyptic wasteland.
